tweets: Samudragupta (r. c. 335–375 CE) expanded Gupta rule across most of the subcontinent — his conquests were so vast that historian V. A. Smith called him the “Napoleon of India.” Yet his gold coins show a gentler feat: seated, playing the vīṇā.

This rare ‘lyrist’ gold coin, struck c. 350 CE, is numismatic proof of a warrior-musician. The Allahabad Pillar inscription, composed by his court poet Harisena, lists the many kingdoms he brought under Gupta rule. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
